title: Effect of membrane surface modification with polyethylene glycol grafting on fouling propensity during β-lactoglobulin ultrafiltration

record.title: Effect of membrane surface modification with polyethylene glycol grafting on fouling propensity during β-lactoglobulin ultrafiltration
record.abstract: Polyethersulphone membranes (10 kDa) were surface-modified by UV-initiated grafting of polyethylene glycol methacrylate (PEGMA) at monomer concentrations of 1, 3, and 5 wt% in aqueous solution. Grafting density was characterised by ATR-FTIR, XPS, and water contact angle measurement. Contact angle decreased from 68° for unmodified membranes to 34° for the 5 wt% PEGMA membrane, confirming increased hydrophilicity. Fouling experiments with β-lactoglobulin (2 g/L, pH 6.8, 50 mM phosphate buffer) at 2 bar TMP showed that total fouling resistance was reduced by 56% for the 5 wt% grafted membrane relative to the control. Pure water flux after a standard NaOH cleaning step was 99.1% recovered for the modified membrane versus 88.4% for the unmodified control. Protein transmission was not significantly affected by grafting at the concentrations tested. Long-term stability of the graft layer over 20 fouling–cleaning cycles was confirmed by reproducible contact angle values.
